passage: Early on Gudi Padwa morning, Mahima Tai swept the yard in front of the village house and handed five-year-old Tushar a small bowl of orange colour. 'Your job: fill every petal on this side.' Tushar crouched, tongue between his teeth, and pinched the colour out slowly. Some fell outside the lines. Mahima Tai didn't fix it. When the neighbours came to look, Tushar stood by his side of the rangoli with orange fingers and announced, 'I made this part.' That night he asked, 'When's the next festival?'

qa.q: What did Mahima Tai hand Tushar?
qa.a: A small bowl of orange colour.

qa.q: What was Tushar feeling when he announced, 'I made this part'?
qa.a: He felt proud and important, having done a real job for the festival.

qa.q: What did Mahima Tai get right in giving Tushar the task?
qa.a: She gave him a clear, real job and didn't fix his mistakes, so that part of the rangoli truly felt like his.

qa.q: How might Mahima Tai feel hearing Tushar ask, 'When's the next festival?'
qa.a: She would likely feel happy and amused, seeing that he now looks forward to festivals.

grounding: Shows a young child given a real part in making a festival rangoli, who is proud of the task and starts looking forward to the next festival.

passage: The week before Lunar New Year, Mr. Chen from the bakery downstairs asked five-year-old Beatriz if she could help. 'Very important job. These lanterns go on the low hooks.' Beatriz stood on a stool, Mamãe holding her waist, and hung six red lanterns one by one, counting in Portuguese. One hung crooked. Mr. Chen left it. All week Beatriz pointed out 'my lanterns' to every customer, and she circled the date on the kitchen calendar with a red crayon.

qa.q: How many lanterns did Beatriz hang?
How did Beatriz feel about 'my lanterns' all week?
qa.a: She felt proud and excited, showing them to every customer as her own work.

qa.q: What made Mr. Chen's invitation meaningful for Beatriz?
qa.a: He called it an important job, gave her a real task at her height and left the crooked lantern, so it truly felt like hers.

qa.q: How might Mr. Chen's customers feel when Beatriz shows off her lanterns?
qa.a: They would likely feel charmed and drawn into the festival mood by her pride.

grounding: Illustrates a young child proud to be given a real task in preparing for a festival, which gives her a place in the community and a date to look forward to.
